semantic_correction.stem: A client with a new stroke needs nursing care, physical therapy, nutrition planning and discharge-resource coordination, and has stated personal recovery goals. Which approach best reflects effective interprofessional collaboration?

options.A: Bring the disciplines and client together to agree on recovery goals, clarify each member's role, and coordinate one plan that reflects the client's priorities.
options.B: Ask each discipline to document its recommendations separately, then have nursing reconcile conflicting goals after the individual evaluations are complete.
options.C: Have the primary provider set the recovery goals, then ask each discipline to adapt its plan to those goals and update the client after the team agrees.
options.D: Begin with the client's stated goals, then let each discipline manage its assigned portion separately and communicate when a conflict or delay appears.

semantic_correction.rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS states that a patient care team is not complete without the patient and that patients and family caregivers contribute to and collaborate in creating the care plan. Team leadership guidance also emphasizes establishing a patient care plan supported by the team, identifying roles and responsibilities, communicating the plan to all team members, and monitoring/modifying it as needed. The TeamSTEPPS brief specifically addresses team membership and roles, clinical status, the care plan, expected outcomes and who will perform each part of the plan. Option A directly integrates the client's recovery goals with shared team goals, clarified roles and one coordinated plan. Option B leaves disciplines working in parallel and reconciles conflicts only afterward. Option C centralizes goal setting in one provider and delays direct client participation. Option D acknowledges client goals but still fragments execution and communication. Therefore A is the uniquely best answer.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Coordinate interprofessional care by including the client in shared goal setting, clarifying team roles and responsibilities, and maintaining one communicated care plan across disciplines.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retained the valid interprofessional-collaboration construct, removed the absolute-word cue and rebuilt all distractors to be plausible coordination alternatives rather than obvious anti-teamwork extremes.

audit_findings_append.finding: The core answer was source-supported, but the original distractors were extreme and one used 'only.' The revised options test realistic differences in interprofessional coordination, shared goal setting and client participation.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0221 tests resolution of informational conflict. V2-Q0124 tests discharge-transition coordination. V2-Q0224 tests formation of a shared interprofessional care plan with direct client participation in recovery goals.

option_audit.A: Correct. It includes the client, establishes shared goals, clarifies roles and coordinates one communicated plan across disciplines.
option_audit.B: Plausible because discipline-specific assessments are needed, but separate planning followed by later reconciliation delays shared goal alignment and coordination.
option_audit.C: Plausible because a primary provider contributes medical goals, but effective interprofessional planning is not a one-provider plan with delayed client participation.
option_audit.D: Plausible because disciplines have distinct responsibilities, but fragmented execution with communication mainly when problems emerge does not create a shared care plan.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. A alone combines direct client participation, shared goals, explicit role clarification and one coordinated plan. B, C and D each omit or delay a core TeamSTEPPS collaboration element.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. All four options are comparable coordination approaches; no absolute-word trap remains and the correct answer is not conspicuously longer.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: Collaborating with multidisciplinary team members and initiating/updating the client plan of care are explicit Management of Care activities for newly licensed RNs.
